parameters.content:
## ops-cost-collector
Every minute: list finished executions through n8n's own API. Executions of workflows with a model node are downloaded (25 per run, oldest first) and every LLM call recorded with its tokens; the rest are marked scanned straight from the listing.

- No workflow needs changing: model nodes already record `tokenUsage`
- Only model sub-nodes are counted; the chain node above repeats the same totals
- Cost isn't stored: the `llm_usage_costed` view prices each call by its day and tier
- Over `daily_budget_usd` today (UTC): one 💸 Telegram message a day, marked sent only after delivery

Successful runs are not saved. Failed runs are, and alert through ops-error-handler.

parameters.query:
-- Postgres node "Scan window" in ops-cost-collector, the first thing every run does.
--
-- 1. Heartbeat: records that the collector ran, even when there is nothing new to scan.
--    Successful runs aren't saved in n8n, and quiet periods record no scans, so without
--    this the dashboard can't tell "nothing happened" from "the collector is dead".
-- 2. Where to start listing executions.
--    Frontier = the newest execution whose data was downloaded (workflow_name is set only on
--    that path; executions of workflows without a model node are marked from the listing and
--    don't move it). Downloads go oldest first, so every LLM execution still waiting is newer
--    than the frontier. Minus 2 h: a run that started earlier but finished after the last scan
--    is still caught.
--    Never more than 1 day back, so the listing stays a few pages: after more than a day of
--    collector downtime, older LLM runs are not counted (decision 032).
WITH beat AS (
    INSERT INTO heartbeats (source, last_beat_at)
    VALUES ('ops-cost-collector', now())
    ON CONFLICT (source) DO UPDATE SET last_beat_at = EXCLUDED.last_beat_at
    RETURNING last_beat_at
)
SELECT to_char(
         (greatest(
             coalesce((SELECT max(started_at) FROM cost_scans WHERE workflow_name IS NOT NULL), '-infinity'),
             now() - interval '1 day')
          - interval '2 hours') AT TIME ZONE 'UTC',
         'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS"Z"') AS started_after,
       (SELECT last_beat_at FROM beat) AS heartbeat_at;

-- Postgres node "Pick unscanned" in ops-cost-collector.
-- $1 = {ids: [...], no_llm: [...]} from "Finished ids".
--
-- 1. Executions of workflows without a model node are marked scanned (0 calls) right here.
-- 2. Of the rest, at most 25 never-scanned ids are returned, oldest first: each needs its
--    full data downloaded, so a backlog is worked off over several runs.
WITH input AS (
    SELECT $1::jsonb AS j
),
mark AS (
    INSERT INTO cost_scans (execution_id, workflow_id, execution_status, started_at, llm_calls)
    SELECT s.execution_id, s.workflow_id, s.execution_status, s.started_at, 0
    FROM input,
         jsonb_to_recordset(coalesce(input.j->'no_llm', '[]'::jsonb)) AS s(
             execution_id text, workflow_id text, execution_status text, started_at timestamptz)
    WHERE s.execution_id ~ '^[0-9]+$' AND s.started_at IS NOT NULL
    ON CONFLICT (execution_id) DO NOTHING
    RETURNING 1
)
SELECT t.id, (SELECT count(*) FROM mark) AS marked_without_llm
FROM input, jsonb_array_elements_text(coalesce(input.j->'ids', '[]'::jsonb)) AS t(id)
WHERE t.id ~ '^[0-9]+$'
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cost_scans s WHERE s.execution_id = t.id)
ORDER BY t.id::bigint
LIMIT 25;

-- Postgres node "Record usage" in ops-cost-collector.
-- $1 = {executions: [...], calls: [...]} from "Extract LLM calls".
--
-- One statement, so calls and the "scanned" marks land together or not at all:
-- an execution is never marked scanned while its calls are missing.
-- Both inserts ignore rows already there, so reading an execution twice changes nothing.

WITH input AS (
    SELECT $1::jsonb AS j
),
calls AS (
    INSERT INTO llm_usage (execution_id, workflow_id, workflow_name, node_name, run_index,
                           provider, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, estimated,
                           execution_status, started_at)
    SELECT c.execution_id, c.workflow_id, coalesce(c.workflow_name, ''), c.node_name, c.run_index,
           c.provider, c.model, c.input_tokens, c.output_tokens, c.estimated,
           c.execution_status, c.started_at
    FROM input,
         jsonb_to_recordset(coalesce(input.j->'calls', '[]'::jsonb)) AS c(
             execution_id text, workflow_id text, workflow_name text, node_name text, run_index integer,
             provider text, model text, input_tokens integer, output_tokens integer, estimated boolean,
             execution_status text, started_at timestamptz)
    ON CONFLICT (execution_id, node_name, run_index) DO NOTHING
    RETURNING 1
),
scans AS (
    INSERT INTO cost_scans (execution_id, workflow_id, workflow_name, execution_status, started_at, llm_calls)
    SELECT s.execution_id, s.workflow_id, s.workflow_name, s.execution_status, s.started_at, s.llm_calls
    FROM input,
         jsonb_to_recordset(coalesce(input.j->'executions', '[]'::jsonb)) AS s(
             execution_id text, workflow_id text, workflow_name text, execution_status text,
             started_at timestamptz, llm_calls integer)
    ON CONFLICT (execution_id) DO NOTHING
    RETURNING 1
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM calls) AS calls_recorded,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM scans) AS executions_recorded;

-- Postgres node "Check budget" in ops-cost-collector, after new usage is recorded.
-- $1 = {daily_budget_usd} from Config.
--
-- Today = the current UTC day. Returns one row only when today's spend is over budget AND
-- no alert for today has been delivered yet; otherwise no rows, and the run ends.
-- The alert row is claimed here and marked sent only after Telegram confirms
-- (mark-budget-alert.sql), so a failed send is retried by the next run, and a sent one is
-- never repeated: one message per day.
WITH input AS (
    SELECT ($1::jsonb->>'daily_budget_usd')::numeric AS budget
),
bounds AS (
    SELECT (now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date AS day,
           date_trunc('day', now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE 'UTC' AS since
),
today AS (
    SELECT coalesce(sum(u.cost_usd), 0)               AS spent,
           count(*)                                   AS calls,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE u.cost_usd IS NULL) AS unpriced,
           count(DISTINCT u.execution_id)             AS runs
    FROM llm_usage_costed u, bounds b
    WHERE u.started_at >= b.since
),
top AS (
    SELECT coalesce(jsonb_agg(t ORDER BY t.cost DESC), '[]'::jsonb) AS workflows
    FROM (
        SELECT u.workflow_name, sum(u.cost_usd) AS cost, count(DISTINCT u.execution_id) AS runs
        FROM llm_usage_costed u, bounds b
        WHERE u.started_at >= b.since
        GROUP BY u.workflow_name
        ORDER BY sum(u.cost_usd) DESC NULLS LAST
        LIMIT 3
    ) t
),
claim AS (
    INSERT INTO cost_alerts (day, kind, threshold, spent)
    SELECT b.day, 'daily_budget', i.budget, t.spent
    FROM bounds b, input i, today t
    WHERE i.budget IS NOT NULL AND t.spent > i.budget
    ON CONFLICT (day, kind) DO UPDATE
        SET spent = EXCLUDED.spent, threshold = EXCLUDED.threshold
        WHERE cost_alerts.sent_at IS NULL
    RETURNING day, kind, threshold, spent
)
SELECT c.day::text AS day, c.kind, c.threshold, c.spent, t.calls, t.runs, t.unpriced, top.workflows
FROM claim c, today t, top;

-- Postgres node "Mark budget alert sent", after Telegram confirmed delivery.
-- $1 = {day, kind} from "Check budget".
UPDATE cost_alerts
SET sent_at = now()
WHERE day = ($1::jsonb->>'day')::date
  AND kind = $1::jsonb->>'kind'
  AND sent_at IS NULL
RETURNING day::text AS day, kind, sent_at;
